## Natural history notes

A tiny yellowish outdoor cockroach characterized by its very small size, pale tan to yellow-brown body, long antennae, and delicate flattened form. In Florida, the Least Yellow Cockroach has been recorded from several counties and is most likely found in warm sheltered microhabitats such as leaf litter, low vegetation, bark, shrubs, and humid natural areas rather than as a typical indoor pest. It feeds as a scavenger on decaying plant material, fungi, algae, and other fine organic debris, helping recycle nutrients while serving as prey for spiders, lizards, birds, and predatory insects.
